newsitem.title: USA: Dow tumbles as US stocks wilt under rate pressures.
newsitem.headline: Dow tumbles as US stocks wilt under rate pressures.

text.p: Wall Street stocks tumbled on Friday, buckling under the mounting pressure of a rapid rise in interest rates.
The Dow industrials slid 157 points to end unofficially at 8031. It was the ninth-largest decline in terms of points in the blue-chip average's history.

As on Thursday, when the Dow fell 71.31 points, stocks were led lower by a slumping bond market, where the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury on Friday jumped to 6.64 percent from 6.53 percent.

"The two props to valuation levels in this market have been interest rates, which have been trending lower, and earnings, which have been surprisingly good," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
"This month, at least so far, we have had the bond market reversing course and nothing sufficiently positive to hold the market up," he said.
The rapid turnaround in interest rates has come amid a sudden flurry of signs that economic growth may have started to accelerate after a tame second quarter.
The evidence, found first in manufacturing and employment reports last week, has sent the long-bond yield climbed 33 basis points from a 1-1/2 year low of 6.31 percent in little more than a week.

Investors, with profits from a four-month, 29 percent Dow rally to protect, moved decisively to do just that on Friday, producing a sell-off that sent blue chips sliding as many as 212 points at its depths.
"The markets have done so well lately," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney. "It doesn't take much to trigger profit-taking."

With little in the way of earnings news to act on, analysts said markets in the coming days would resume their obsessive search for any sign of accelerating inflation. Wholesale and consumer price reports are both due next week, meaning more jittery action could lie ahead.
The rising interest rate climate hit financial shares hard on Friday. Among banks, NationsBank Corp fell 2-5/8 to 66, BankAmerica Corp fell 2-1/4 to 68-1/4, and Citicorp fell 2-1/2 to 134.

Among individual issues, Heritage Media Corp climbed 2-3/16 to 19-1/16 after news that the U.S. Justice Department would not oppose the company's acquisition by Australian media conglomerate News Corp Ltd.
American Depositary Shares in News Corp, listed on the New York Stock Exchange, eased 3/8 to 17-5/8.
Electronic Data Systems Corp slid 6-1/16 to 37-1/8 after the computer services company reported weaker-than-expected earnings. The results prompted a wave of rating downgrades by Wall Street firms.

Coca-Cola Co fell 3-13/16 to 62-3/4 after the Dow component said it expected third-quarter earnings would show only a slight improvement from the year-ago period. Analysts expressed concern that a strong dollar was dragging the beverage company's results.
Cymer Inc jumped 3-9/16 to 81-1/8. Late Thursday, Cymer declared a two-for-one stock split
The S&P 500 index fell 17.65 points to 933.54.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 25.66 points to 1598.52.
